_comment: DESIGN.md §3, §8, §9. Waves 1-25 authored; the scaling factors apply only past wave 25, which the Final Showdown makes academic. Boss waves carry only their escort here - the boss is drawn from bossBank at run time (§3.4). All placeholders.

showdown._comment: §3.3, replaced. The attrition endgame is gone. The last monster wave is afterWave; clearing it moves every surviving army into the cross arena for a free-for-all. approachDepth is the open ground between a player's build grid and the centre square, so a spoke is buildZone.depth + approachDepth long and the centre is buildZone.width on a side. dampening scales healing, summon HP and crowd-control durations down by perSecond per second once graceSeconds have passed, so a fight cannot run forever. All placeholders.

centre._comment: KING OF THE HILL. Whichever army has the MOST living bodies inside the centre square holds it, and every one of that army’s bodies - wherever it is standing - deals damageDealt more damage and takes damageTaken less. A tie is held by everyone tied, so contesting it is never worse than conceding it. Without this the arena rewards exactly one strategy: mass the slowest, longest-ranged units you can afford, let the other three fight, and walk in to mop up. A reason to stand in the middle is a reason to own a front line. Percentages, in the same convention as an ability’s modify effect: 0.5 is +50%, -0.5 is -50%.

showdown._sightNote: LINE OF SIGHT. The arena is a cross, and the four corners of its bounding square are not arena: nothing stands there and nothing walks there. With this on they are not transparent either - a body cannot shoot through one, so the back of the south spoke cannot draw a bead on the back of the east spoke across the gap between them. Off, the corners are glass, and a long enough gun covers two spokes from a standing start while nothing can walk to it. A switch rather than a constant so the difference can be measured rather than assumed.

acquire._comment: How far a unit looks for something to fight in the arena, edge to edge in tiles: its own reach plus margin, never less than minimum. Nothing looks across the whole board - a unit with nothing inside this walks at the centre instead, which is what makes four armies converge rather than each pick a duel from thirty tiles away. The lane's equivalent is lane.monsterAcquireRange. Placeholders.

enrage._comment: Additive, not compounding: multiplier = 1 + ratePerSecond * secondsEnraged. rate 0.03 is derived from the doc's worked example (60s in = 2.8x). Applies to monster damage, move speed and attack speed - never to HP.

scaling._comment: hp and damage compound EVERY wave from wave 1 (§9.1, amended) - steeply to wave 10, because that is where the economy compounds fastest and a player who invests early must not be able to outgrow the waves; then by `after` from wave 11, because past that an army grows by about what a wave pays and the early rate would outrun every army there is (docs/BALANCE.md §4). count and bounty apply only past the last authored wave.

bossScaling._comment: Per BOSS WAVE, compounded: wave 5 draws the bank as authored, wave 10 gets it once over, and from wave 15 each boss grows by `after` instead - faster, because past wave 10 an army grows faster than the flat bounty and a boss that did not keep up would be one large monster. The bank is four bodies of EQUAL power in four armour types, so this is the whole of what separates a late boss from an early one.

_clockNote: DESIGN CHANGE to §3.2: there is no global wave-spawn clock. The only global timers are this 30s build phase and the enrage clock (§8). Combat runs until every living lane is empty, so a second wave can never land on an unfinished one.
_ladderNote: WAVES 1 TO 10 ARE TUNED and carry `armyGold`: each was measured with `npm run waves` until an average army worth that much gold beat it with nothing leaking, three quarters of that mostly could not, and half could not at all; then waves 1 to 10 were played whole with `npm run runs` to check a greedy economy cannot outgrow them (docs/BALANCE.md §4a). They run 22 to 45 bodies. WAVES 11 TO 25 ARE STALE. They were authored against monster stats that have since been cut - a grub was 45 health and is now 30 - so they are both weaker than they were and short of the 25-45 bodies the tuned ladder runs at. They were left alone rather than mechanically rescaled: those waves are built from swarm bodies and need HEAVIER monsters and a theme each, not more of the same. That is composition work, not arithmetic. Tune 11 to 25 the way 1 to 10 were tuned before trusting any of them.
